title: Multilayer membrane and local fibrous-shell foundation
purpose: Verify the reusable kinematic, constitutive, multilayer-lowering, and result-identity foundation required before a global fibrous-shell element or forming procedure can be promoted.
physics: finite-kinematics woven-reinforcement membrane and local fibre-specific shell response

execution.evidence: Analytical local channel checks plus a loaded finite-kinematics membrane solve and unified result-output check run in serial.

observables: Objective director-shell and fibre-curve measures under superposed rigid rotation.
Independent membrane, transverse-shear, in-plane-bending, and normal-bending energies, resultants, and tangent blocks.
Nine-component UFL stored energy and its automatically differentiated generalized resultants.
Stable computational-layer and physical-layer identities for varying-orientation stacks.
Per-layer DG result fields, aggregate stored energy, and the exact layer-to-field manifest from a completed model.step result.
acceptance: The three-dimensional surface deformation lift maps both reference tangents and the reference normal and transforms objectively.
Pure local shell channels remain independent, carry symmetric positive-semidefinite tangents, and sum to total stored energy.
UFL differentiation of the symbolic generalized stored energy recovers the nine explicit conjugate resultants component by component.
A membrane stack adds only compatible energy scalars and never combines generalized resultants expressed in unlike fibre frames.
Same-orientation grouping scales energy, conjugate resultants, and tangent by the number of explicitly listed physical layer IDs and rejects duplicate IDs.
A loaded multilayer membrane converges through the standard Step and writes collision-free per-layer strain, resultant, direction, and energy fields.
The in-plane membrane provider refuses every nonzero bending block rather than silently discarding shell mechanics.
limitations: This benchmark does not contain a global shell element, boundary moment, or transverse-slip solve.
It does not validate tool contact, friction, inter-ply slip, wrinkling, explicit quasi-static controls, or a physical drape experiment.
MPI field identity and public shell benchmarks remain promotion gates for the future global provider.
